dataflow.summary: Restricted manager -> settings route -> bot-visible channel list -> persisted destination -> Discord send.

reachability.summary: Reachable with Manage Server and an explicit private-channel View Channel denial.

confidence.rationale: The GET and PUT routes share a helper that only checks bot-visible channels.

findings.remediation: Resolve the authenticated guild member and require their effective ViewChannel permission for every returned and submitted channel.

rootCause.summary: Guild-level Manage Server authorization was treated as permission to see and target every channel visible to the bot.

severity.rationale: An authenticated restricted manager can discover private channels and cause Duck to publish configured content or logs there.

findings.summary: Dashboard channel lists and destination validation use Duck's visibility but omit the requester's effective View Channel permission.
findings.title: Manage Server users can enumerate and target channels they cannot view

validation.summary: Validated by tracing settings GET/PUT from OAuth guild permission checks through getGuildTextChannels to stored welcome and logging destinations.

dataflow.summary: Rotating public addresses -> request key insertion -> process-lifetime Map growth.

reachability.summary: All public routes reach the limiter before authentication.

confidence.rationale: The early return directly bypasses every eviction branch.

findings.remediation: Prune and cap the map on every path before returning, and add a global request ceiling independent of client identity.

rootCause.summary: Attacker-keyed state is bounded only on the repeated-key path, not before every insertion.

severity.rationale: Unauthenticated rotated source addresses can grow process memory until service degradation.

findings.summary: The limiter returns immediately after inserting a new key, skipping its own pruning and 10,000-entry cap.
findings.title: Rate-limit state grows without bound for new source addresses

validation.summary: A unique remoteAddress and route bucket always executes set followed by return while map size is unchecked.

dataflow.summary: Authenticated requests -> Discord fetch -> pending handlers and response buffers.

reachability.summary: Reachable after normal Discord OAuth authentication, especially during upstream degradation.

confidence.rationale: Every reviewed Discord fetch lacks AbortSignal, bounded response reads, and in-flight accounting.

findings.remediation: Add abort deadlines, byte-limited JSON reads, refresh deduplication, and global/per-session in-flight limits.

rootCause.summary: Inbound socket limits were present, but dependency work had no corresponding deadline, response-size, or concurrency policy.

severity.rationale: A malicious authenticated user can amplify Discord latency into process exhaustion.

findings.summary: OAuth and authenticated guild requests can accumulate unbounded pending outbound fetches and JSON response work.
findings.title: Discord API calls lack application deadlines and concurrency bounds

validation.summary: Authenticated /api/guilds calls each start a fresh fetch and response.json without application bounds.

dataflow.summary: Repeated violating messages -> warning push -> full JSON rewrite and full-history formatting.

reachability.summary: Reachable by non-exempt guild members when AutoMod or a custom warn action is enabled.

confidence.rationale: The mutation is an unconditional array push and all existing limits apply only to separate runtime maps.

findings.remediation: Retain a bounded number of warnings per member and bounded warned-member counts per guild and globally; normalize legacy data during load.

rootCause.summary: Persistent warning arrays have no per-member, per-guild, or global retention policy.

severity.rationale: An unmanageable guild member can drive persistent disk, serialization, and response amplification over time.

findings.summary: AutoMod and custom actions append warnings indefinitely and rewrite or display the full history.
findings.title: Persistent warning histories grow without a retention bound

validation.summary: Repeated automatic warnings reach addMemberWarning even when Discord hierarchy prevents the configured escalation from removing the sender.

dataflow.summary: Concurrent manager checkouts -> multiple Stripe subscriptions -> signed events -> last accepted guild subscription record.

reachability.summary: Requires fresh Manage Server authorization and completing competing Stripe subscription flows.

confidence.rationale: The source establishes the race; practical impact depends on checkout completion and Stripe delivery order.

findings.remediation: Persist and lock pending checkout ownership, bind a guild to one subscription ID, and reconcile webhook state against Stripe's canonical subscription snapshot.

rootCause.summary: Checkout has no pending lock, while webhook state accepts any supported subscription for the guild and compares only second-resolution event times.

severity.rationale: A guild manager can create competing flows whose valid events corrupt entitlement and portal ownership.

findings.summary: Concurrent pre-activation checkouts and equal-second webhook delivery are not bound to one canonical subscription identity.
findings.title: Competing Stripe subscriptions can overwrite one guild entitlement

validation.summary: Multiple sessions can be created before any webhook marks the guild active; later valid events overwrite subscriptionId and customerId.

dataflow.summary: Cross-site navigation or crawler -> GET donation route -> Stripe session creation.

confidence.rationale: Static donation links directly target the GET side-effect route.

findings.remediation: Use a same-origin POST interaction and a strict billing-specific plus global creation limit.

rootCause.summary: A resource-creating operation was modeled as a crawlable GET and given the generic public rate limit.

severity.rationale: Cross-site pages and crawlers can create abandoned sessions and consume outbound/provider capacity, but cannot charge users.

findings.summary: Donation links expose provider-side resource creation through an unauthenticated safe-method route in the broad web rate bucket.
findings.title: Public GET requests create Stripe Checkout sessions

validation.summary: Any GET with one of six allowed amounts immediately invokes stripe.checkout.sessions.create.

dataflow.summary: Cached former permission -> settings GET -> per-guild settings and metadata response.

reachability.summary: Requires membership or permission revocation within the cache window.

confidence.rationale: The GET route explicitly uses guildAccess's non-fresh default.

findings.remediation: Refresh Discord authorization for tenant-scoped settings reads.

rootCause.summary: A latency cache for guild lists doubles as the authorization source for tenant-sensitive reads.

severity.rationale: Revoked users can briefly read tenant settings and metadata but all writes already refresh authorization.

findings.summary: Settings GET reuses a 30-second cached Discord guild permission snapshot.
findings.title: Recently revoked managers retain a brief settings-read window

validation.summary: After /api/guilds populates the cache, settings GET does not call Discord again for up to 30 seconds.
